name: InstructRAG: Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Instruction Graphs for LLM-Based Task Planning
venue: SIGIR 2025 (Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval); preprint arXiv:2504.13032. DOI: 10.1145/3726302.3730009. Accepted as Oral / full-score paper.
authors_affiliation: Zheng Wang, Shu Xian Teo, Jun Jie Chew, Wei Shi — all at Huawei Singapore Research Center, Singapore.
code_url: N/A (no official public code repository released; the author's homepage lists only Paper/Slides/Media links for this paper, with no Code link. The popular GitHub repo weizhepei/InstructRAG is a DIFFERENT, unrelated ICLR 2025 paper 'Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-synthesized rationales' and must not be confused with this work.)
task_domain: LLM-based task planning / agent planning. Spans multi-hop QA reasoning (HotpotQA), embodied tasks (ALFWorld), web shopping (Webshop), and scientific reasoning (ScienceWorld). Framed as grounding the thought-action-observation (TAO) planning process via RAG.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-step agent planning following the thought-action-observation (TAO) / ReAct paradigm, where retrieval grounds the LLM's generation of thoughts and actions. Supervision is available: the method is trained offline on 'seen' tasks (split into support set for graph construction and query set for agent training) and then few-shot adapts to 'unseen' tasks. It is a multi-agent system (two cooperating learned agents: an RL-Agent and an ML-Agent) sitting around a single planner LLM (which may be trainable, e.g. GLM-4, or frozen, e.g. GPT-4o mini, DeepSeek-V2). Meta-learning setup with explicit train/few-shot-adapt/test stages.
what_is_retrieved: Instruction paths — i.e., ordered sequences of correct past actions (instructions such as Search[Scott Derrickson], Lookup[nationality], Goto[shelf 6], Take[vase 2]) drawn from successful past task-solving experiences. New paths can also be composed by traversing/combining instructions across graph nodes (enlargeability), so retrieved paths need not have existed verbatim in the database.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / induced memory of the agent's own past successful experiences (an instruction graph built offline from a support set), which is further EXPANDED at few-shot-adaptation time when the testing support set is inserted into the graph. It is not an external static document corpus or KB; it is a self-constructed episodic-experience store. Best characterized as a growing experience memory (induced offline + extended at adaptation time), not a frozen external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: The RL-Agent retrieves K candidate instruction PATHS (K=3 by default, a tunable hyperparameter), then the ML-Agent selects exactly ONE single best path to inject as the planning exemplar. So the operative objective is precision-driven single-best-path selection (1 of K) optimized by downstream end-to-end task metric, rather than a fixed top-k list returned to the LLM or an explicit minimal-set-completeness objective. The path itself must be complete enough to solve the question, but the retrieval target is the single most effective path.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (retrieve/compose instruction paths for a new question). Reuse: yes (selected path injected as an ICL exemplar/plan into the prompt). Revise: partial — new paths are composed by recombining instructions during graph traversal, but there is no per-instance LLM adaptation/repair of a retrieved case at inference. Retain: partial — successful paths are stored at construction and the graph is extended with the testing support set, but there is no online retention of newly solved query-set cases during deployment. Flags: [Retrieve, Reuse, partial-Revise, partial-Retain].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed as RAG-for-task-planning within a multi-agent meta-reinforcement-learning framework. It realizes some CBR-like mechanisms (retrieve-and-reuse of past solution paths, composition of new solutions) under different terminology (instruction graph, enlargeability, transferability).
retrieval_unit: Instruction path = a full (or composed sub-)trajectory of discrete actions, i.e., a workflow-routine / action-sequence. The atomic stored element is an instruction (a single action like Search[topic]); paths over these instructions (organized as graph nodes of clustered instructions and edges of tasks) are the retrieval unit. So: sub-trajectory / workflow-routine of actions, retrieved as a path over a KG-style instruction graph.
index_source: Growing memory induced offline from the training support set's successful instruction paths (graph constructed once during data pre-processing), then further extended at few-shot-adaptation time by inserting the testing support set into the graph (G -> G'). Not a static external corpus; not grown from query-set/test-query solutions online.
index_structure_topology: A directed instruction GRAPH G(V,E). Each node is a SET of similar instructions (clustered via AKNN + cosine-similarity threshold delta); each edge is a SET of tasks (with associated questions) that traverse between two instruction nodes. Nodes act as junctions enabling new path combinations. This is a graph/dependency topology over actions, distinct from a flat vector index.
retriever_type: Hybrid: AKNN dense-embedding similarity search (HNSW, Malkov & Yashunin) for instruction matching + graph traversal (DFS) controlled by a LEARNED RL policy (the RL-Agent) that decides node inclusion/exclusion, followed by a LEARNED dense bi-encoder selector (the ML-Agent, CLIP-style text encoders) for final single-path selection. So: dense + learned-policy + learned-bi-encoder hybrid.
retriever_learning_signal: Two learned components with distinct signals. (1) RL-Agent: trained with downstream-task-effectiveness as RL reward — warm-start via binary cross-entropy on on-path/off-path node labels, then policy gradient (REINFORCE) where the reward r = Delta(A-hat, A) is the end-to-end LLM answer quality (e.g., F1 on HotpotQA). (2) ML-Agent: contrastive learning (InfoNCE-style QPA loss + QPM binary-classification loss in pre-training; fine-tuning uses contrastive loss with the best end-to-end-scored path as positive and hard negatives from the K retrieved paths). Both are meta-learned (MAML-style) for fast adaptation. So: RL/value-from-downstream-effectiveness for the policy + contrastive (similarity + downstream-best) for the selector.
query_construction: The raw input question Q-hat is the query. For the RL-Agent's MDP state, the query embedding v_{Q-hat} is compared (cosine similarity) against (a) the most similar instruction in a node, (b) the most similar task on the in-edge (task embedding = average of its questions' embeddings), and (c) the most similar question within the closest task. For the ML-Agent, the question is encoded by a transformer text encoder ([EOS]-token representation) and matched against path encodings. No explicit sub-query decomposition or synthetic query expansion.
query_granularity: Task-level / question-level (one query per input question Q-hat at planning time). There is also a two-level structure internally (a per-node step-level RL traversal decision builds paths, and a path-level selection), but the externally issued query is at the question/task level, issued once before planning.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (plan-time): for each input question, the RL-Agent retrieves K candidate paths and the ML-Agent selects one path, which is injected into the prompt up front to guide the entire TAO planning sequence. Retrieval is not re-triggered per TAO step at inference.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule — retrieval is performed once per question at planning time (no token-confidence, uncertainty, reflection-token, or agent-initiated dynamic trigger). Internally the RL-Agent's per-node include/exclude decision is governed by its learned policy over cosine-similarity states, but this is path construction, not a learned WHEN-to-retrieve trigger.
reranking: Effectively yes: a two-stage selection. Stage 1 the RL-Agent retrieves/builds K candidate paths via learned graph traversal; Stage 2 the ML-Agent (a learned CLIP-style bi-encoder, meta-learned) acts as a learned reranker/selector that picks the single most relevant path by question-path cosine similarity. Not a classic cross-encoder; it is a learned bi-encoder selection trained with contrastive + downstream-effectiveness signals.
retrieved_context_refinement: Selection/reranking down to a single best path (decompose-then-recompose at the graph level: instructions are recombined into new paths, then one path is selected). No reason-in-documents distillation or compression of the path text itself; the selected path is injected as a structured plan. Noise is handled implicitly via diverse instruction combinations rather than an explicit relevance-filter module.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — instructions/actions are not tool docstrings; they are action templates (e.g., Search[topic], Lookup[entity], Goto[loc], Take[obj]). Instruction text is embedded directly (via the embedding model used for AKNN) and clustered into nodes by cosine similarity with threshold delta=0.4; no synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field tool embedding.
index_content_separation: Partial/implicit. The graph stores lightweight instruction nodes and task edges (keys for retrieval); the heavier content (instruction definitions, demonstrations) is assembled into the prompt only after a path is selected. There is no explicit progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content mechanism described as such.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — no live tool index, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool integration protocol. The 'instructions' are environment actions in ReAct-style task environments, not external API tools. The graph is static after offline construction except for the one-time extension with the testing support set at adaptation time.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial in a planning (not tool) sense: predefined transition rules may constrain the RL-Agent's action space (e.g., on HotpotQA, disallow Lookup before a Search on the topic — following KnowAgent), capturing prerequisite/ordering constraints between actions. The graph edges also encode legal action transitions. But there is no tool-dependency graph, shared-auth, or bipartite tool KG.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation as a planning exemplar. The single selected instruction path P-hat is written into a 4-part prompt: (1) Task Description (the question), (2) Instruction Definitions (semantics of each action type), (3) Planning Path (the retrieved/composed path as a structured step-by-step plan), and (4) Demonstrations (example planning paths). The LLM then generates the answer following the TAO process grounded in this plan. The path's downstream effectiveness is also fed back as the RL-Agent reward (training signal).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan with one-shot exemplar injection: the RL-Agent + ML-Agent retrieve and select a path BEFORE the LLM plans, and that path is provided as an in-context plan/exemplar guiding the whole TAO rollout. Not interleaved per-step at inference, not inside MCTS/tree search at planning time. (Internally the RL-Agent does a DFS tree traversal over the instruction graph to build candidate paths, but that is the retrieval module, separate from the LLM's planning.)
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-question (one retrieval-and-selection per question, then the LLM completes the full TAO plan). Retrieval is not woven per-CoT-step, per-sentence, or per-tool-call at inference time.
adaptation_mechanism: Primarily verbatim-ICL-exemplar reuse of the selected path, augmented by graph-level recomposition (new paths are synthesized by combining stored instructions across junction nodes via RL-guided traversal, enabling coverage of questions never seen verbatim — 'enlargeability'). No per-instance LLM-prompted rewriting or execution-feedback repair of an individual retrieved case at test time; adaptation to new tasks is via MAML-style few-shot meta-update of the two agents' parameters.
retrieved_item_representation: A free-text structured planning path (an ordered sequence of action instructions, e.g., Search[..]->Lookup[..]->Search[..]->Lookup[..]) injected as the 'Planning Path' section of the prompt, alongside instruction definitions and demonstrations. It is a free-text workflow/plan, not a latent token, not an executable program.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: A reusable workflow / action-sequence routine (mid-level): more abstract than a single demonstration (it is a composable path that can be recombined across tasks) but still concrete action-level instructions rather than a distilled natural-language strategy or guideline.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Robustness arises from the diverse instruction combinations enabled by the graph plus the learned RL-Agent path-construction and ML-Agent path-selection, which help pick appropriate paths and downweight bad ones; the agents are trained against downstream effectiveness (reward = answer quality), implicitly disfavoring paths that yield poor answers. Demonstrated empirically: with 50% erroneous historical paths injected, InstructRAG's F1 drops only ~11.1% (37.17 -> 33.04) vs. RAP dropping from 29.82 -> 21.72. No explicit self-reflection relevance evaluator or distractor-aware SFT module.
memory_type: Graph-structured experience memory (an instruction graph of past successful action paths) — i.e., a workflow/procedural memory organized as a directed graph (nodes = instruction sets, edges = task sets). Best tagged: graph + procedural/workflow.
write_back: Yes, but only at construction/adaptation time, not during deployment inference. Successful instruction paths from the training support set are written into the graph during offline construction, and the testing support set's paths are inserted into the graph (G -> G') during the few-shot adaptation stage. New query-set solutions produced during testing are NOT written back into the graph.
online_growth: No (not during test-time inference). The store grows in two discrete offline/adaptation phases (initial offline construction from training support set; one-time extension with the testing support set at few-shot adaptation). It does not continuously grow from solved test queries during deployment.
write_back_trigger: On-success only, at dataset-preparation/adaptation time: only instruction paths that correctly solve their question (verified against ground truth) are inserted into the graph. There is no per-step, reflective, or human-validated online write trigger during inference; failed paths are excluded from the clean graph (and are only added artificially in the noise-robustness experiment).
failure_experience_usage: Success-only for the memory store: the graph is built from correct/successful instruction paths only; failed paths are deliberately excluded (failed paths are injected only in the noise-robustness stress test, not used as a learning signal). However, the ML-Agent's contrastive fine-tuning uses hard NEGATIVES (the non-best among the K retrieved paths and paths from other questions) as a discriminative signal, and the RL-Agent learns from low rewards on poor paths — so negative/failure signals are used in TRAINING the retrievers, but failed experiences are not stored as retrievable corrective rules.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only with dedup-style merging into node sets: new instructions are either merged into an existing similar node (if cosine similarity >= delta, e.g., identical instructions merge with similarity 1.0) or create a new node (if < delta); tasks are appended to edge sets. Existing stored instructions/paths are not mutated, refined, overwritten, or pruned/forgotten. The graph topology grows monotonically; trainable agent parameters (not memory entries) are what get updated via meta-learning.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes. Retrieval is explicitly a LEARNED policy: the RL-Agent models graph traversal as a Markov Decision Process and learns pi_theta(a|s) (include/exclude node) via warm-start (BCE) + REINFORCE policy gradient with end-to-end reward; the ML-Agent learns a contrastive selection policy; both are meta-trained (MAML, Finn et al. 2017). This is decidedly NOT fixed similarity top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No cross-agent/cross-framework memory sharing in the collective-memory sense. It is a multi-agent system (RL-Agent + ML-Agent cooperating around one planner LLM via a shared reward loop), and the single instruction graph is shared between these two cooperating modules, but there is no sharing of memory across multiple independent agents or heterogeneous agent frameworks. Memory is a single shared private store for one InstructRAG instance.
benchmarks: HotpotQA (multi-hop QA, ~113K Wikipedia QA pairs; F1), ALFWorld (embodied household tasks; success rate), Webshop (web-shopping navigation; reward 0-1), ScienceWorld (elementary-school scientific reasoning; reward 0-1, used for cross-dataset generalization with training on HotpotQA).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (HotpotQA); embodied (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld); web (Webshop). Mix of multi-hop QA, embodied, and web-agent families.
baselines: ReAct, WKM (World Knowledge Model), Reflexion, GenGround, and RAP (Retrieval-Augmented Planning; identified as the best baseline). All run on the same three backbone LLMs (GLM-4, GPT-4o mini, DeepSeek-V2) with matched retrievers/setups. WKM not reported on HotpotQA.
key_metrics: F1 score (HotpotQA), success rate (ALFWorld), reward score 0-1 (Webshop, ScienceWorld). Plus runtime/efficiency: graph construction time (s), training time (hours), few-shot adaptation time (mins/task), testing time (s), and number of graph nodes. All main results reported statistically significant (t-test, p<0.05).
headline_result: Up to 19.2% improvement over the best existing approach (RAP) on HotpotQA. Concretely, on unseen tasks: improvements of 19.2% (HotpotQA), 9.3% (ALFWorld), and 6.1% (Webshop) over RAP. Best absolute numbers with DeepSeek-V2 on unseen tasks: HotpotQA F1 37.17 (vs RAP 29.82), ALFWorld success 81.34 (vs RAP 72.39), Webshop reward 74.00 (vs RAP 72.72).
ablations: Component ablation on HotpotQA (DeepSeek-V2, F1=37.17 full): w/o Instruction Graph 32.87 (graph contributes ~11.6%); w/o RL-Agent 33.45 (RL-Agent ~11.1%); w/o warm-start in RL-Agent 34.37; w/o policy gradient in RL-Agent 36.18; w/o ML-Agent 34.78 (ML-Agent ~6.9%); w/o pre-training in ML-Agent 36.19; w/o fine-tuning in ML-Agent 36.24. Parameter studies: threshold delta swept 0.0-1.0 (best at 0.4, F1=37.17; #nodes grows 5->725; delta=1.0 collapses graph to individual paths losing recombination), and K (candidate paths) swept 1-5 (F1 converges at K=3=37.17; testing time grows with K). Noise robustness (Table 4): stable up to 50% erroneous paths (only -11.1%). Cross-dataset generalization (Table 2): HotpotQA->ScienceWorld beats RAP by 6-10%. Seen-task gains (Table 3): +21.9%/+10.8%/+10.4%. Few-shot scaling (Fig 2): effectiveness stable across #tasks; converges around 80% of samples.
evaluation_decoupling: No — the paper reports end-to-end task metrics (F1 / success rate / reward) only. It does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k, nDCG, or path-retrieval-completeness reported separately). The RL reward is itself the end-to-end metric, so retrieval quality is measured only through downstream task performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Predominantly outcome-only (final answer F1 / task success / reward). No separate process-quality metrics such as reasoning faithfulness, step-wise retrieval accuracy, or trajectory-quality scoring are reported; intermediate path quality is captured only implicitly via the end-to-end reward used to train the agents.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported runtime/efficiency (Table 6, DeepSeek-V2 HotpotQA, delta=0.4): graph construction ~20.87s (one-time), training ~23.93 hours, few-shot adaptation ~27.10 mins/task (tasks parallelizable; ~27.1 min avg per task), testing ~34.74s. Table 7: testing time grows with K (32.05s at K=1 to 42.09s at K=5) while F1 peaks at K=3; K=3 is the accuracy/cost sweet spot. LLM I/O is cached during training to boost efficiency. No API-dollar-cost or token-savings figures reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval of K=3 candidate paths (tuned; converges at 3), then exactly ONE selected path injected into the prompt. The prompt is a fixed 4-part structure (Task Description, Instruction Definitions, Planning Path, Demonstrations). No explicit token-budget cap or reranked-then-truncated scheme; effectively a single-path budget. graph construction threshold delta=0.4; RL-Agent reward discount 0.99, lr 0.001.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — this is a method paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A — uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one. (Context: HotpotQA ~113K QA pairs; meta-learning task splits defined per dataset, e.g. HotpotQA's 12 answer types split 6 seen / 6 unseen; Webshop split 60% categories train / rest test; ALFWorld uses its provided seen/unseen split; ScienceWorld used entirely as unseen cross-dataset transfer.)
builds_on: ReAct / thought-action-observation (TAO) planning paradigm (Yao et al. 2022b); RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024, retrieval-augmented planning over stored experiences) as the closest predecessor it improves on; MAML model-agnostic meta-learning (Finn et al. 2017) and meta-ICL methods (MetaICL/MAML-en-LLM/MTIL) for transferability; REINFORCE (Williams 1992) for the RL policy; CLIP-style dual text encoders (Radford et al. 2021) for the ML-Agent; HNSW/AKNN (Malkov & Yashunin 2018) for instruction indexing; KnowAgent (Zhu et al. 2024) for action-transition rules. Also relates to the authors' own RAG line (M-RAG ACL'24, EMG-RAG EMNLP'24).
contrasts_with: RAP (stores past experiences as independent context/action-observation trajectories and retrieves by AKNN similarity without enlargeability/transferability — InstructRAG instead organizes them in a recombinable graph and learns retrieval); GenGround (generate-then-ground for multi-hop reasoning, search-engine dependent); PlanRAG (plan-then-retrieve, decision-QA / video-game domain specific); RAT (iterative CoT revision); plain prompting/fine-tuning planners ReAct, Reflexion, WKM, FireAct, NAT, ETO that are bounded by the LLM's own knowledge and do not leverage a structured retrievable experience store.
lineage: Sits in the experience/memory-augmented LLM-planning lineage (Group C: RAG planning) — a structured-memory planner that retrieves over an induced graph of past task paths and adds a learned RL retrieval policy + meta-learned selector. Bridges retrieval-augmented planning (RAP/RAT/GenGround/PlanRAG) with multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning, distinguished by (i) graph-organized recombinable instruction paths (enlargeability) and (ii) MAML-based fast task transfer (transferability).
